meta.name: RF28R7351SR French Door Refrigerator
meta.summary: 28 cu ft French-door refrigerator with Twin Cooling, a full-width Flex Zone drawer, ice and water dispenser and an inverter (BLDC) compressor on R600a. Error codes from Samsung; test modes and check values from a sister model's troubleshooting manual. 3D model drawn to the published outside dimensions; internal parts placed from the service manual figures.

components.name: Cabinet shell
components.desc: Insulated outer cabinet. Front corners carry warm refrigerant pipe to stop condensation, so they feel warm. Outside: 908 W × 1,778 H (1,749 without hinges) × 746 mm deep without doors, 927 mm with doors.

components.name: French doors and gaskets
components.desc: Two fridge doors; the left door holds the dispenser and ice maker. Gaskets must seal fully or fans frost up.

components.name: Flex Zone drawer
components.desc: Full-width middle drawer (3.8 cu ft) with its own temperature setting, fed by a motor damper.
components.src: Samsung RF28R7351 service manual (summary and contents)

components.name: Freezer drawer
components.src: Samsung RF28R7351 service manual (summary and contents)

components.name: Display panel (panel PCB)
components.desc: Blue LED touch display on the door; shows error codes and is used for test, load and diagnostic modes.
components.src: Samsung RF28R7351 service manual (summary and contents)

components.name: Ice and water dispenser
components.desc: One-lever dispenser in the left door, with the ice route motor and dispenser panel PCB.
components.src: Samsung RF28R7351 service manual (summary and contents)

components.name: Ice maker and ice room
components.desc: In-door ice maker with its own ice room fan, ice bucket and ice duct/pipe heaters.
components.src: Samsung RF28R7351 service manual (summary and contents)

components.name: Water filter
components.desc: Slim filter between the crisper drawers.
components.src: Samsung RF28R7351 service manual (summary and contents)

components.name: Fridge evaporator and fan
components.desc: Fridge-side evaporator (Twin Cooling) and fridge fan behind the rear cover. Fan fault shows 22E/22C.
components.src: Samsung RF28R7351 service manual (summary and contents)

components.name: Freezer evaporator and fan
components.desc: Freezer evaporator with its fan and defrost heater. Fan fault shows 21E, usually from frost.
components.src: Samsung RF28R7351 service manual (summary and contents)

components.name: Motor damper (Flex Zone air)
components.desc: Opens and closes cold air to the Flex Zone.
components.src: Samsung RF28R7351 service manual (summary and contents)

components.name: Defrost heaters and sensors
components.desc: Freezer and fridge/Flex defrost heaters with defrost sensors and a bimetal thermal protector (opens at 60 °C/140 °F, closes at 40 °C/104 °F).
components.src: Samsung RF28R7351 service manual (summary and contents)

components.name: Inverter compressor
components.desc: Reciprocating BLDC compressor NF54M7151AN/E01, R600a (70 g). Driven by the inverter PCB.
components.src: Samsung RF28R7351 service manual (summary and contents)

components.name: Condenser and compressor-room fan
components.desc: Condenser and machine-compartment cooling fan at the bottom rear. Dust here causes warm temperatures.
components.src: Samsung RF28R7351 service manual (summary and contents)

components.name: Inverter PCB
components.desc: Drives the compressor; source of compressor current, stall and voltage errors (83E, 84C, 85E, 86E).
components.src: Samsung RF28K9380/RF22K9381 troubleshooting manual (sister model — verify on this model's tech sheet)

components.name: Electric box (main PCB)
components.desc: Main PCB and power supply (SMPS) that read the sensors and drive fans, heaters, valves and the damper. Position approximate.
components.src: Samsung RF28R7351 service manual (summary and contents)

components.name: Water valve and tank
components.desc: Inlet water valve feeding the filter, water tank, dispenser and ice maker.
components.src: Samsung RF28R7351 service manual (summary and contents)

components.name: Temperature sensors
components.desc: Thermistors for freezer, fridge, Flex Zone, defrost, ambient, ice maker and ice room. Read as a voltage at the main PCB.
components.src: Samsung RF28K9380/RF22K9381 troubleshooting manual (sister model — verify on this model's tech sheet)

faults.title: Freezer fan error
causes: Fan blocked by frost (door left open, gasket gap)
checks: Make sure the freezer drawer closes and the gasket seals all round
Manually defrost (unplug with doors open for a few hours) and see if it returns
Sister model: fan supply at the main PCB fan connector should be 7–12 V when running
faults.src: Samsung support: refrigerator error codes; Samsung RF28K9380/RF22K9381 troubleshooting manual (sister model — verify on this model's tech sheet)

faults.title: Fridge fan error
causes: Fridge door left open long enough to frost the fan
checks: Unplug, leave the doors open a few hours to thaw, then restart
If it returns: fridge fan supply 7–12 V when running (sister model)
Check the fridge door gaskets
faults.src: Samsung support: refrigerator error codes; Samsung RF28K9380/RF22K9381 troubleshooting manual (sister model — verify on this model's tech sheet)

faults.title: Defrost sensor error
causes: Defrost sensor open or shorted, or its connector loose
checks: Sister model: sensor reads open above 100 kΩ, shorted below 2 kΩ
Check the sensor voltage at the main PCB sensor connector (about 1.0–4.5 V when good)
faults.src: Samsung support: refrigerator error codes; Samsung RF28K9380/RF22K9381 troubleshooting manual (sister model — verify on this model's tech sheet)
faults.safety: Unplug the refrigerator before measuring resistance; the inverter and power supply carry line voltage.

faults.title: Ice maker (freezer) sensor error
causes: Ice maker sensor open or shorted
checks: Check the sensor and its wiring; replace the sensor or ice maker as needed
faults.src: Samsung support: refrigerator error codes

faults.title: Ice maker sensor error
causes: Fridge ice maker sensor fault or wiring
checks: Sister model: ice maker sensor voltage about 1.0–4.5 V at the main PCB
Replace the ice maker sensor
faults.src: Samsung support: refrigerator error codes; Samsung RF28K9380/RF22K9381 troubleshooting manual (sister model — verify on this model's tech sheet)

faults.title: Ice pipe heater error
checks: Sister model: ice duct heater about 135 Ω ±7% (unplugged)
Check the heater connector
faults.src: Samsung support: refrigerator error codes; Samsung RF28K9380/RF22K9381 troubleshooting manual (sister model — verify on this model's tech sheet)
faults.safety: Unplug the refrigerator before measuring resistance; the inverter and power supply carry line voltage.

faults.title: Ice maker function error
causes: Ice maker jammed (ice clumps) or its motor/switch failed
Water not reaching the ice maker
checks: Clear any ice jam and reseat the ice bucket
Check water supply and the filter
Sister model guidance: replace the ice maker, reconnect power and recheck
faults.src: Samsung support: refrigerator error codes; Samsung RF28K9380/RF22K9381 troubleshooting manual (sister model — verify on this model's tech sheet)

faults.title: Ice room fan error
causes: Ice room fan frosted or failed
checks: Check the ice room door seal
Sister model: ice room fan supply 7–12 V when running
faults.src: Samsung support: refrigerator error codes; Samsung RF28K9380/RF22K9381 troubleshooting manual (sister model — verify on this model's tech sheet)

faults.title: Water in the Autofill compartment
causes: Water leaking into the Autofill pitcher compartment
checks: Follow Samsung's leak guide: check the Autofill pitcher seating and lines
faults.src: Samsung support: refrigerator error codes

faults.title: Compressor abnormal current
checks: Power off at the breaker for 60 seconds, restore, and see if it returns
Check the compressor wire connections at the inverter
Sister model: check the inverter's DC 15 V output (fault if under 13.5 V)
faults.src: Samsung support: refrigerator error codes; Samsung RF28K9380/RF22K9381 troubleshooting manual (sister model — verify on this model's tech sheet)
faults.safety: Unplug the refrigerator before measuring resistance; the inverter and power supply carry line voltage.

faults.title: Compressor lock (stall)
checks: Check the outlet voltage under load
Reset by removing power for 60 seconds
If it repeats, the compressor or inverter needs a technician
faults.src: Samsung support: refrigerator error codes; Samsung RF28K9380/RF22K9381 troubleshooting manual (sister model — verify on this model's tech sheet)
faults.safety: Unplug the refrigerator before measuring resistance; the inverter and power supply carry line voltage.

faults.title: Compressor low voltage (brown-out)
causes: Supply voltage dropped (sister model trips at about 106 VAC or lower)
checks: Measure outlet voltage while the compressor starts
Plug directly into a dedicated outlet
Reset by removing power for 60 seconds
faults.src: Samsung support: refrigerator error codes; Samsung RF28K9380/RF22K9381 troubleshooting manual (sister model — verify on this model's tech sheet)

faults.title: Compressor over-voltage (surge)
checks: Reset by removing power for 60 seconds
If frequent, have the circuit checked
faults.src: Samsung support: refrigerator error codes

faults.title: Communication error at start-up
causes: Power interrupted while the controls were booting
checks: Remove power for 60 seconds and restore
If it returns, check the main-to-panel harness
faults.src: Samsung support: refrigerator error codes

faults.title: Panel communication error
causes: Loose harness between the door panel and main PCB (connector above the door hinge)
checks: Power off, disconnect and reconnect the harness above the door, restore power
Sister model: if the cable is good, the main or panel PCB is replaced
faults.src: Samsung support: refrigerator error codes; Samsung RF28K9380/RF22K9381 troubleshooting manual (sister model — verify on this model's tech sheet)
faults.safety: Unplug the refrigerator before measuring resistance; the inverter and power supply carry line voltage.

faults.title: Display shows OF OF / not cooling (demo mode)
causes: Cooling Off / Demo / Shop mode turned on
checks: Hold the top two left-side buttons for 5–8 seconds until a chime sounds
Some models need the top right button too
Check it doesn't come back
faults.src: Samsung support: refrigerator error codes

faults.title: Fridge or freezer too warm
causes: Temperature set too high, or Energy Saver on
Unit in sun or near heat, or too little clearance
Condenser dusty or compressor-room fan stopped
checks: Check the set temperatures and Energy Saver
Check clearance: 2 in at top and rear, 3¾ in at the sides
Clean the condenser area and check the fan runs
Look for frost on the rear covers (defrost problem)
faults.src: Samsung RF28R7351SR user manual; Samsung RF28R7351 service manual (summary and contents)

faults.title: Fridge freezing food
checks: Raise the setting
Keep food away from the vents
Check the Flex Zone temperature setting
faults.src: Samsung RF28R7351SR user manual

faults.title: Refrigerator not running at all
causes: Power cord loose or breaker tripped
checks: Check the plug and breaker
Check for any display on the panel
faults.src: Samsung RF28R7351SR user manual

faults.title: No ice or slow ice
causes: Water tank or filter frozen or blocked
checks: Wait 12 hours after emptying the bucket
Check the Ice Maker Off icon and freezer setting
Check the water supply and filter
faults.src: Samsung RF28K9380/RF22K9381 troubleshooting manual (sister model — verify on this model's tech sheet)

sequence.name: Power-up self-check
sequence.desc: After plugging in or an outage, all icons flash while the controls run a self-diagnostic, then normal display returns.

sequence.name: Cooling
sequence.desc: Main PCB reads the cabinet sensors and runs the inverter compressor and fans at the speed needed.

sequence.name: Flex Zone control
sequence.desc: The motor damper and Flex fan meter cold air into the Flex Zone drawer to hold its selected mode.

sequence.name: Defrost
sequence.desc: Automatic defrost: freezer every 12–23 h, fridge every 6–11 h. Heaters run until the defrost sensor ends the cycle; a bimetal protector cuts out at 60 °C as a backup.
sequence.ends: Defrost sensor reaches its end temperature

sequence.name: Ice making
sequence.desc: The ice maker fills, freezes with the ice room fan, and harvests into the bucket; heaters keep the duct and bucket from freezing up.

sequence.name: Dispensing
sequence.desc: Pressing the lever opens the water valve or runs the ice route motor.

checks.name: Installation checks
checks.why: Poor clearance and leveling cause warm temperatures and door seal problems.
steps: Level, hard floor rated for 660 lb
Clearance: at least 2 in at top and rear, 3¾ in at the sides
Keep away from direct sun and heat sources
checks.src: Samsung RF28R7351 service manual (summary and contents); Samsung RF28R7351SR user manual

checks.name: Clean the machine compartment
checks.why: Dust on the condenser and fan makes the compressor work harder.
steps: Remove the rear lower cover and vacuum the condenser and fan
Check the compressor-room fan spins freely

checks.name: Door gasket check
checks.why: Leaking gaskets frost the fans (21E/22E) and warm the cabinet.
steps: Close each door on a strip of paper; it should hold firmly all round
Clean gaskets with mild soap; replace if torn

checks.name: Water filter replacement
checks.why: An old filter slows water and ice.
steps: Replace the filter at the interval in the user manual, or when the filter indicator asks
Flush water through the dispenser after replacing

checks.name: Read stored error codes (sister-model button combos)
checks.why: Shows codes that come and go.
steps: Hold Freezer + Fridge for 6 s until the screen blinks; keep holding until errors show
Load mode: hold Freezer + Fridge + Flex Zone for 6 s to see which loads are on
Test mode: hold Freezer + Flex Zone for 6 s, then step through forced modes with Flex Zone; FD forces defrost
Confirm the button combinations on this model's tech sheet (inside the unit) before relying on them
checks.src: Samsung RF28K9380/RF22K9381 troubleshooting manual (sister model — verify on this model's tech sheet)

checks.name: Power reset
steps: Unplug or switch off the breaker for 60 seconds, then restore
Don't unplug just to clear other codes: it can hide the cause

reference.name: Specifications
rows: 27.93 cu ft: fridge 15.71, freezer 8.42, Flex Zone 3.80
Twin Cooling with Surround Multi Flow
35¾ in W × 36½ in D (with handles) × 70 in H
notes: R600a is flammable: sealed-system work needs a technician certified for hydrocarbon refrigerants.

reference.name: Sensor and load check values
reference.intro: From the sister model's troubleshooting manual; confirm on this model's tech sheet.
rows: About 1.0–4.5 V at the main PCB sensor connector
Ice duct, ice bucket, door heaters
15 V nominal; fault if under 13.5 V
notes: Measure DC voltages to the PCB's GND point, not the chassis.

reference.name: Error code quick list
notes: Request service for any code not listed.

devices.func: Reads sensors, runs fans, heaters, damper, valves and the compressor command
Switching power supply for the control boards (line voltage present)
Freezer, fridge, compressor-room and Flex fans
Ice duct, ice bucket and door heaters
Communication and run command to the inverter PCB (44 on sister model)
Harness to the door display (PC ER when loose)

defects.name: Ice clumps or ice stuck in the bucket
defects.looks: Cubes fused together; dispenser won't push ice.
isolate: Check whether ice is used regularly

causes.cause: Ice not used for long periods
Ice bucket or duct heater failed
causes.fix: Check heater resistance (about 135 Ω on the sister model)

causes.cause: Door opened often in humid conditions

defects.name: Slow or no water from dispenser
isolate: Check flow with the filter removed (bypass if supported)

causes.fix: Raise the fridge temperature slightly; let it thaw
Check supply pressure and the saddle valve

defects.name: Frost inside the freezer drawer
defects.looks: Frost on food and drawer walls.
isolate: Check the drawer closes fully and the gasket seals

causes.cause: Drawer left open or blocked by food
